name: GGUF Q6_K (6-bit K-quant)
quality_delta: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.35 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.03, within noise); unweighted mean 69.23 vs 69.47; size 6283 MiB (-58.98%). GSM8K reported 58.98 vs 77.63 for F16, which is a 18-point drop inconsistent with a +0.03 perplexity change and with the paper's own claim that Q6_K is near-baseline - treat the Q6_K GSM8K cell as unverified.
notes: Q6_K has no S/M/L variant: 6-bit elements over a 256-value super-block with per-16 sub-block scales quantized to 8 bits. Effectively the last 'no visible loss' tier before Q8_0. Weight-only: activations stay in FP16/BF16 at runtime, so there is no '4-bit activations with hardware support' claim to make here. ggml has bespoke dequantize+gemm kernels per type, but no accelerator has a GGUF/k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM explicitly labels its GGUF support experimental and under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool (quant-vllm-gguf-doc). Cost is real though: in llama.cpp's Llama-3.1-8B table Q6_K decodes at 58.67 tok/s vs Q8_0's 50.93 and F16's 29.17, so it is not free - and the study's Pareto analysis explicitly finds Q6_K and Q8_0 *dominated* by Q5_0 (less reduction AND higher AvgLoss).
